## What this does

One freshness semantics, stated once and shared — every value evaluated at
a named instant, every unevaluable surface honest about it.

- **One shared verdict (SIG-TRANSP-029).**
  `policy.freshness.freshness_verdict(cadence…, executions, at)` is the
  single pure function the exporter, the status lane and ACT-02's alerting
  consume: closed vocabulary (`on_time`/`late`/`overdue`/`never_run`/
  `last_run_failed`/`not_scheduled`/`one_time_load`/`not_applicable`),
  documented precedence (static classes → never_run → last_run_failed →
  overdue → late → on_time), the C-7 `run_record_missing` flag, and
  `evaluated_at` on every verdict. `freshness_state`/`FreshnessState`
  remain as delegating aliases — one implementation, never a dual-run.
  `freshness_issue_class` is the one verdict→issue mapping the exporter's
  issue rows and the alerting path share; the issue emitter now consults
  it instead of a hard-coded state set. `include_next_fire` gates
  `next_scheduled_day` to the status lane — release emitters never
  request it, so no release artifact can carry a reader-clock value.
- **Volatility over ALL published claims (SIG-TRANSP-030, K9 §5.2).** Two
  new `TRANSPARENCY_QUERIES` reads (`freshness_predicates`,
  `freshness_observations`) measure every publishable-eligible claim —
  the dated-only/site-only bias dies. Each source's freshness row emits
  the registry-class `distribution`, the dominant class with its
  half-life, and `unregistered_predicate` — claims on predicates the
  registry does not declare are counted, never silently dropped. The
  P35.20b declared-class staleness gate is unchanged: a declared class is
  never replaced by a vote.
- **Staleness honesty (SIG-TRANSP-030, F-137).** Each deduped latest
  dated observation per (source, subject, predicate) ages against its
  predicate's half-life at `at` → `evaluable`/`stale`/`dated_unevaluable`.
  A freshness row emits `stale n` only when evaluable observations exist —
  an unevaluable source carries `evaluable`/`not_evaluable` counts, never
  "0 stale", never "unknown". The web page renders "stale n of m
  evaluable" and "+ m undated".
- **Two change dates (SIG-TRANSP-031, K9 §5.4).** `last_upstream_change`
  is the newest upstream-DECLARED instant across capture marks
  (`editingInfo.lastEditDate`, `rowsUpdatedAt`/`dataUpdatedAt`,
  `metadata_modified`, `data_last_updated`, `Last-Modified`) with its
  declared basis named — else a `records_digest` diff on flushed marks —
  else `not_detectable` (a token-only publisher like ETag declares a
  version, never a date; the retrieval clock is never substituted).
  `last_sig_records_change` diffs `records_digest` where comparable,
  else carries J3's labelled interim "last run that added claims — not a
  content-change measure" until P36.68's release-slice diff lands.
  `order_capture_records` marks a byte-only diff `formatting change
  only` — it never moves the date.
- **Connector capture side.** New `connectors/upstream_modified.py`:
  `upstream_declared` reads platform metadata (one bounded, deduped GET
  per platform doc per run through the shared fetcher — robots, rate
  limits and per-fetch telemetry bind it like every egress), then
  payload-declared fields (EoF `data_last_updated`), then the S-14
  header lane (`Last-Modified` instant / `ETag` token). Probe failures
  degrade to honest absence — never run-fatal, never a guessed date.
  `CaptureRef` carries the declared triple (never part of the content
  address); resume/replay round-trips it; `procurement._merge_pages`
  forwards response headers. `records_digest` =
  `claim_set_fingerprint(claims, classes=predicate_temporal_classes())`
  rides the flushed mark only — `FetchRecord` gains the run-level
  combined digest + `capture_upstream[]`.
- **New sqitch `capture_freshness_marks`.** `ingest_run_capture` gains
  `records_digest`, `upstream_modified_at`, `upstream_token`,
  `upstream_modified_basis`; CHECK keeps `records_digest` flushed-only;
  `v_transparency_capture` gains all four appended to its explicit-column
  list (sig_export surface only); NULL-tolerant for pre-change marks — no
  backfill invents a declared value. `PgClaimSink.record_capture` and the
  resume-marks read carry the columns with a savepoint-bounded legacy
  fallback on `UndefinedColumn` — a spine one migration behind still
  records marks; constraint violations still propagate.
- **Cadence disclosure (SIG-TRANSP-007).** The declared rule rendered to
  day granularity ("monthly, day 6") with its basis named
  (`ops/cadence.toml` / `registry, not scheduled` / `not_recorded`);
  `one_time_load` is a first-class verdict and schedule facet; the
  `_UNSET` sentinel distinguishes an unreadable cadence doc
  (`not_recorded`) from an explicitly empty one.
- **Two clocks (SIG-TRANSP-034's release side).** Release pages evaluate
  the verdict at the release as-of (`spine_export` derives it
  `dataset.as_of → generated_at → now`); every freshness value carries
  `evaluated_at` (freshness rows, the shaped `FreshnessRow`, the web
  page's own disclosure naming the release clock vs the reader's). No
  release artifact carries a now-dependent value (next run, current
  verdict).

## What this does not do

- No status lane — P36.43 owns it; this row lands the shared function and
  the release-side two-clocks rule.
- No sources-table render — P36.48 owns the K9 columns.
- No per-source slice diffs — P36.68 owns them; the SIG-records date
  carries the labelled interim basis.
- No PKG-10 dating rule change — P35.20b's fail-closed gate stands.
- No production mutation — the connector roll (OM-20 named mutation) is
  pre-authorised (the GATE-G4 §4 list names P35.41 verbatim) but deferred
  under OM-19: it runs on `r11/P35.41-freshness-live` inside the AR-3
  window with the AR-2 restore point first. No rights flip, no gate
  tick, no `ingestion_permitted` change, no outside contact.

## Deviations

- `transparency_sources` emission is unchanged; the shared verdict lives
  in `freshness.jsonl` rows and the sources row's two change-date fields
  (K9 C-6 — the same field, not a new one).
- `_RESUME_MARKS` degrades to no-resume on `UndefinedColumn` (a spine one
  migration behind) rather than querying a legacy column set — the
  existing `UndefinedTable` precedent: resume is an optimisation, never
  correctness (re-fetch dedupes on content identity).
